title: Drywall Repair Cost in 2026
description: Drywall repair cost in 2026 by hole size and damage type, with DIY vs pro prices, minimum fees, and texture costs.

cover.alt: Illustration of a drywall sheet with screws on a concrete & walls blueprint background with a measuring tape

takeaways: Angi puts single repairs at $20 to $200 by hole size in 2026, but most pros charge a $350 to $650 minimum per visit on HomeGuide.
Water damage and ceiling repairs cost the most, at $600 to $1,550 and $220 to $1,300 on Angi 2026 data.
Batch every small hole, dent, and nail pop into one visit, because one trip fee beats four separate calls.
body:
Drywall repair cost in 2026 depends less on the hole and more on the visit. Angi's 2026 data puts a pro repair at $150 to $1,800 overall, with small holes at $20 to $120 and large holes at $50 to $200 before texture and paint. HomeGuide tells the other half of the story: most contractors charge a $350 to $650 minimum per job, and its finished patch prices run $300 to $500 for a small hole and $500 to $800 or more for a large one. Both sets of numbers are real. The first is the repair line item, and the second is what a single small job costs once a pro drives out, sets up, and comes back for a second coat.

## Drywall repair cost by type of damage

Use this table to place your damage in a band, then read the minimum fee note below it. Texture matching and paint are often extra, and they are the lines that decide if a repair vanishes or shows from the doorway.

| Type of damage | Angi 2026 range | What drives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nail pops | $10 to $60 | Screw, mud, sand, touch-up |
| Small holes, up to 4 in | $20 to $120 | Patch or filler, one or two coats |
| Dents and tears | $20 to $150 | Fill, sand, prime so the patch does not flash |
| Large holes, 5 in and up | $50 to $200 | Cut-out patch, backing, tape, three coats |
| Cracks | $60 to $400 | Tape and mud, or a sign of movement |
| Ceiling repairs | $220 to $1,300 | Overhead work, slower coats, bigger setups |
| Water damage | $600 to $1,550 | New board, insulation check, mold check |

Angi lists ceiling work and water damage far above flat wall patches, and the reason is labor, not material. A bucket of compound is cheap. Working overhead on a ladder, or opening a wall to confirm the leak is fixed and the cavity is dry, is not. HomeGuide puts ceiling repairs at $350 to $1,500 or more, close to the same band once minimum fees and return trips are counted.

Per square foot pricing shows up on big sections. Angi notes large hole work at $50 to $75 per square foot in some quotes, while full section replacement is more often quoted as a flat job price. If a wall needs a full new sheet, price it as new work with our [drywall calculator](/blog/drywall-calculator/) for sheets, mud, and tape, then add finishing labor on top.

## Worked example: three holes in one visit

Say a hall wall has one doorknob hole at 6 in across, plus two small anchor holes at 1 in each. You want the wall smooth, textured to match, primed, and ready for paint, all in one visit.

Price the line items from the Angi ranges first:

- Large hole: $50 to $200.
- Two small holes: 2 x $20 to 2 x $120 = $40 to $240.
- Line item sum: $50 + $40 = $90 low, and $200 + $240 = $440 high.

Now apply the real-world floor. HomeGuide says most contractors charge a $350 to $650 minimum job fee, and its finished prices are $300 to $500 for one small hole and $500 to $800 or more for a large hole job. So a fair quote for this bundled visit should land near $350 to $650, not near $90. The gap is the trip, the setup, the drying time, and the second visit for the finish coat and sanding.

Check the math a second way. If the handyman rate is $60 per hour and the job takes 2 hours on day one plus 1.5 hours on day two for sanding, texture, and cleanup, labor is 3.5 x $60 = $210, plus patch material, compound, tape, and primer at about $40, for $250 before the firm adds its minimum and travel. That path also lands in the $350 area once the minimum applies. Round your budget up to $500 and you will not flinch at a fair quote. Doing the same three holes yourself costs a $10 to $30 repair kit on Angi figures, plus compound and a can of spray texture if you need it, often under $60 total if you own a putty knife and sander.

## What pushes the price up or down?

Texture is the silent line item. Smooth walls are the easiest to hide a patch in. Orange peel, knockdown, and skip trowel textures need spray or hand work to blend, and a patch that is flat but wrong-textured reads like a billboard under side light. Ask if texture matching is in the quote or extra, and get the answer in writing.

- Location matters. Ceilings cost more than walls, and high stairwell walls cost more than either, due to ladder and plank setups.
- Water damage costs more because the source must be fixed first, wet board and insulation come out, and the cavity must dry before new board goes in.
- Paint adds a step. Priming is not optional on fresh compound, since unprimed mud flashes through finish paint as dull spots. Full wall repaint costs more than a touch-up that may not match sheen.
- Access and timing matter. One hole in an empty rental between tenants is fast work. The same hole behind a bookcase in a lived-in home is not.

Cracks need a cause check before a price means much. A hairline crack at a door corner is normal settling in many homes. A crack that reopens after repair, runs on a diagonal, or comes with a sticking door can point to movement that mud will not fix. Pay for the patch once you know the cause, not twice. Price paint after the repair with the [cost to paint a room guide](/blog/cost-to-paint-a-room/).

## DIY patch or hire a pro?

Do it yourself for nail holes, anchor holes, small dents, and clean small holes in low-light walls. A self-stick mesh patch, compound in thin coats, and patience between coats will beat most rushed jobs. Keep coats thin. Two thin coats sand in minutes, while one fat coat dries slow, shrinks, and cracks.

Hire a pro for large holes, ceiling damage, water damage, and any patch in a bright living room where the wall gets raking light from a window. Pros feather compound wider, often 12 to 18 in past a large patch, and that wide blend is the skill you are paying for. Hire out texture-heavy walls for the same reason.

Skip DIY entirely if you find mold growth over a wide area, soft board that crumbles, or damage near electrical panels and wiring you do not understand. Open the wall only when power is off at the breaker and you know what is behind the board. Cut with a shallow blade, check with a flashlight first, and never force a saw where pipes or cables may run. For popcorn texture on the ceiling above the repair, read our [popcorn ceiling removal cost guide](/blog/popcorn-ceiling-removal-cost/) before you scrape anything in an older home.

## How to get a fair quote and save

Batch the work. Walk the whole house with painter's tape, mark every hole, dent, pop, and crack, and hand the pro one list. Ten small repairs in one visit cost far less per repair than three separate calls, because the trip fee is paid once. This is the single best saving on this page.

Send photos with a tape measure next to each hole for scale. A pro can quote small work from clear photos. Ask three things in writing: does the price include texture, does it include prime and paint or prime only, and how many visits will it take?

Time the repair with painting you already plan. A patch primed and painted as part of a room repaint avoids the touch-up mismatch problem and the separate minimum fee. Pay on completion, after you have checked the wall in daylight and at an angle with a lamp, since side light tells the truth about patches.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to patch a small hole in drywall?
Angi lists small holes up to 4 in at $20 to $120 as a line item, while HomeGuide puts a finished small patch at $300 to $500 once minimum fees are counted. Expect a real single-visit quote near the HomeGuide end, and a per-hole price near the Angi end when many holes are done in one visit.

### Why is there a minimum fee for a tiny repair?
Travel, setup, drop cloths, and a return trip for the finish coat take the same time for a 1 in hole as for a 6 in hole. HomeGuide puts most contractor minimums at $350 to $650. Batching several repairs into one visit is how you make that fee worth paying.

### How much does ceiling drywall repair cost?
Angi lists ceiling repairs at $220 to $1,300, and HomeGuide at $350 to $1,500 or more. Overhead work is slower, coats sag if they are rushed, and water stains on ceilings often mean a leak check above. Get the leak fixed first or you will pay for the same patch twice.

### Does drywall repair include painting?
Often not. Many quotes cover patch, sand, and sometimes primer only. Touch-up paint can flash if the old paint has faded, so pros may quote a full wall repaint as an extra. Our [primer calculator](/blog/primer-calculator/) helps you count primer if you finish the wall yourself.

### How long does a drywall repair take?
The hands-on time for a small patch is under an hour, but drying rules the schedule. Most repairs need two or three coats with drying between them, so pros split the job over 2 visits in 1 to 3 days. Fast-setting compound can cut that to one long visit on small work.

### Should I repair or replace a damaged drywall section?
Replace the section when board is soft, moldy, or water-soaked, because compound cannot restore strength to failed board. Patch when the board around the damage is firm and dry.

## Next step
Mark every repair in the house with tape, take photos with a tape measure for scale, and get two quotes for the full list at once. If new board is part of the plan, count sheets and mud first with our [drywall calculator](/blog/drywall-calculator/).

*Prices are US figures from 2026 and vary by region and supplier.*
